units: <cite ref="Niddah 12a:28">Nidd. 12ᵃ</cite> <he>כל … נקרא צ׳</he> he who fulfils the words of the scholars is called discreet (pious).
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Demai 6:5:5">Y. Dem. VI, 25ᵈ</cite> top (ref. to <he>צְנוּעֵי</he> Mish.
Dem. VI, 6) שהכשר נקרא צ׳ the worthy man is called tsanuʿa.
<cite ref="Berakhot 62a:6">Ber. 62ᵃ</cite> <he>צ׳ בבית הכסא</he> decent in his manners in the privy.
<cite ref="Berakhot 62a:15">Ib.</cite> <he>צ׳ באורחותיו</he> decorous in his ways; a. fr.—Pl. <he>צְנוּעִים</he>, <he>צְנוּעִין</he>.

<cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 6:6:1">Cant. R. to VI, 6</cite> (ref. to <he>רחלים</he> <cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 6:6:1">ib.</cite>) <he>מה רחל זו צנועה כן היו ישראל צ׳ וכ׳</he> as the lamb is pure, so were the Israelites pure and virtuous in the Midianitic war.
<cite ref="Mishnah Demai 6:6">Dem. VI, 6</cite> <he>צְנוּעֵי בית הלל</he>, v. <cite ref="K01326"><he>כָּשֵׁר</he> II</cite>.
Maas. Sh. V, 1 הצ׳ מניחין וכ׳ the conscientious lay money aside &c.; a. fr.—Fem. צְנוּעָה.
<cite ref="Shabbat 53b:20">Sabb. 53ᵇ</cite> <he>כמה צ׳ אשה זו</he> how chaste was this woman! Cant. R. l. c., v. supra; a. fr.—Pl. <he>צְנוּעוֹת</he>.
<cite ref="Ketubot 2b:14">Keth. 2ᵇ</cite>, sq. <he>משום צ׳</he> for the sake of the virtuous women, opp. <he>פרוּצות</he>.
